en: Chapter XIV: An Instruction on the Ritual for the Worship of Vajrayoginī.
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain that which was requested by Vajrayoginī:
having worshipped the external yoginīs, it is not possible to wander through the sacred seats (pīṭhas). || 14.1 ||
Vajrayoginī, wandering among the yogins.
Having worshipped the Yoginī in one's own home, one should perform the preliminary service (*pūrvasevā*) and so forth;
without the preliminary service, his ritual action is in vain and his effort is wasted.
Without the Yoginī,
[it is] in vain; [otherwise it is] suffering.
On the tenth day of the dark fortnight and likewise on the tenth day of the bright fortnight,
one should extend an invitation with a focused mind, employing various purificatory rites and other such methods.
With a mind that is dark, conditioned, and impure.
One should worship the goddesses in one's own home, facing the east, according to the proper method.
Saffron, collyrium, and vermilion powder for the crest.
In one's own home,
one should worship the goddesses.
*saṃsthitaḥ*: *sasthitaḥ* (A), *saṃsthitaṃ* (L) *kuṅkumaṃ*: *kuṅkuma* (A), *kuṅkumaṃ* (L) *kajjalaṃ*: *karjjalaṃ* (A), *kajjaran* (L)
And indeed,
all vermilion powder.
One should worship the head, hands, feet, and face with ointments;
the head should be adorned with hanging garlands and perfumed with fragrant incense.
And indeed,
eight faces.

Indeed, the donors, out of faith, [bestowed] specifically one, two, three, four, five, seven, nine, and up to twenty-four [villages]. || 14.6 ||
Four,
nine,
[and] givers.
One should prepare food, drink, and beverages accompanied by fish and meat;
one should cultivate the mantra and the mudrā, and display the secret signs of the heroes.
One should meditate upon the mantra and the mudrā; one should meditate upon and worship the mudrā of the hero’s convention (*vīrasaṃketa*).
One should visualize oneself in the form of Vajravairocanī and always worship the deity;
preceded by the offering of bali, one should present the sacrificial pap and the lamp.
One should worship Vajrayoginī accompanied by songs of praise. || 14.8 ||
The form of the mudrā,
the deity,
was presented.
These Yoginīs, who are joined together and closely united, should be worshipped with diligent effort.
And by means of liquors and even meats, the Vajra goddesses are worshipped by the devoted person who has attained delight in the illustrious Vajrayāna.
Those whose minds are contented become givers of boons; for boons are held in their hands. || 14.9 ||

For one possessed of devotion,
having attained the state of Vajrayāmā, with a mind full of contentment, [he attains] delight in the Vajrayāna.
Those situated in the hands, those situated in the time-periods,
the excellent ones, the powerful ones.
(Quoted in the Ācāryakriyāsamuccaya)

The Vajra goddesses are to be worshipped swiftly with effort, even with liquors and meats. When they are worshipped by a person possessed of devotion who has attained delight in the illustrious Vajrayāna,
they become satisfied in heart and grant boons, for the boons are held within their hands.
Through the yoga of the glorious Heruka, the Mothers are pleased by him.
One should perform the worship of the Mothers, the Nimitas, and the Yoginīs, as well as rites for pacification and nourishment. || 14.20 ||
The worship of the Yoginīs by means of signs (*nimittaiḥ*);
[the rite of] nourishment (*pauṣṭika*) is performed with nourishing substances; and at the moment of the libation to Kaumārī, the fruit of action—whether auspicious or inauspicious—is determined.
Kaumārī [or Komārī], in the act of satiation, with two hands, by means of which he was not satisfied in his mind. || 14.21 ||
Is it crushed? It has been crushed by him;
consequently, a recurrence of the disease arises and you shall experience suffering.
(The word *roga* [disease] is written as *roma* [hair]).
Laughing, he emits a sound; one should worship him at that very moment.
There is no doubt that the disease will become incurable, even for one protected by the *Rabhibīta-tantra*. (14.22)
Whatever Dharma is bestowed upon the two eyes when one is exhorted and honored, it should always be understood as the essential means for accomplishment, as spoken by Kaṇa and Malaṇa. || 14.23 ||
Bringing them face to face, he brings each pair together individually.
Kali is always indicated as being everywhere Kaumārī. (14.24)
The yogi should look at his back; he should place [his hand] upon his teeth and nails. Again, karmas arise, for there is no satiety from eating meat. 14.25.
There is no satisfaction with food or drink, nor with jewels from any quarter;
diseases arise unexpectedly, as do injuries from weapons, tigers, and the like.

The wise man should observe that frequent singing and playing of instruments, as well as repeated laughing and smiling, indicate fear of kings and thieves; this is the manifestation of the Kaumārī [śakti].
Having drunk intoxicants, they dance many times over; one should observe that great diseases and fears will befall them at the times of worship. (14.28)
One should look in all directions for all kinds of food and edibles scattered about;
for it is held that the deities are provoked by the faults committed by those who act improperly.
But if they engage in conversation with one another or laugh with one another, the maiden Kaumārī, perceiving a lapse in their ritual performance, shall give birth to splendors. (A 41r, 14.30)
When being enjoyed,
if she turns her back while moving, O beautiful one, it indicates the onset of the disease of madness.
He performs further action and becomes afflicted with chronic disease;
he stamps his foot upon the ground for the purpose of abandoning his position. (14.32)
At the time of worship, however, possession is indicated by the mutual embrace [of the deity];
this sign of accomplishment through worship is free from such transformations.
Therefore, the practitioner should always observe with diligence the worship;
one should worship the Vajra-yoginīs, who bestow the fruit of all desires. 14.34.
